ellie: Ran a 1h perf run against `kvspan` with variable seqlen mix (32/512/2048). HBM bandwidth spikes start around 45m and correlate with KV eviction waves. attaching nsys: /mnt/traces/1952109876-kvspan-nsys.qdrep :eyes:

omar: Can you paste the nsys command you used? want to reproduce locally.

jess: quick glance at perfetto shows alternating memcpy peaks and small kernels. maybe kernel selection falling back to elementwise kernels for large seq splits.

ellie: nsys command was: ```nsys profile -o /mnt/traces/1952109876-kvspan -t cuda,cudnn,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none --cpuctx-mode=cpu Sampling``` ran the workload via the longseq stress runner.

omar: thx. do you have the kernel timeline snippet? curious about which kernels align to HBM peak.

ellie: pasted a trimmed timeline (nsys GUI exported):
```
00:45:12.120 memcpyHtoD  HBM  3.2GB/s  (preload chunk)
00:45:12.312 conv_fused_kernel  1.1GB/s
00:45:12.316 kv_read_page  HBM  8.9GB/s  (burst)
00:45:12.340 transpose_tile  4.5GB/s
00:45:12.341 evict_page  HBM  7.8GB/s
00:45:12.345 small_elementwise  0.2GB/s (lots of short calls)
```

jess: that `kv_read_page`/`evict_page` burst pattern is the tell. looks like when seqlen crosses the microbatch boundary we lose aggregated KV spans and re-request pages.

omar: hypothesis: batching heuristic splits tokens such that KV pages partially overlap across requests and we don't coalesce reads. That increases random HBM reads -> thrash.

ellie: agreed. i instrumented runtime: when batch boundary hits mid-page we fall back to per-request page fetch. sample log: `KVFetch: page_id=42 range=[1024..3072] requester=shard-3 coalesce=false`.

jess: interesting — does the kernel selector prefer a kernel variant that expects contiguous KV in VRAM? fallback kernels might be doing scatter loads. Could explain memcpy + small kernels.

omar: next steps: 1) re-run with `--kv-coalesce=true` toggle to verify. 2) capture perfetto with CPU stacks to see scheduler related stalls. 3) try a patched kernel selector that prefers tiled-read fused path for large seqlen.

ellie: ran step1: `--kv-coalesce=true` reduces HBM peaks by ~38% for the 2048 seqlen cases. baseline: 9.1GB/s peak -> patched: 5.6GB/s. traces at /mnt/traces/1952109876-coalesce.qdrep

jess: nice! any throughput/latency tradeoff? did we see increased CPU overhead for coalescing?

ellie: small cpu overhead (~3% more CPU time) but tail latency improves 12ms median -> 8ms. Seems like net win.

omar: small typo in name, but good result. can we add a microbenchmark that simulates worst-case page misalignment and include it in nightly perf suite?

jess: yes i'll add `kvspan_misaligned_bench` to perf suite. i'd like a guard in kernel selector: if seqlen variance > X and page_miss_rate > Y, force coalesce path.

triage-bot: Incident created: RT-1952 "KV page thrash under long-seqlen mixtures" linked to traces /mnt/traces/1952109876*. Assigned: eng-runtime oncall.

ellie: i'll open a PR with the runtime metric (page_miss_rate) + config flag. putting draft in https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4123 :pt_lightning:

omar: once PR lands let's run a 4-node soak with dedicated GPU to validate steady-state. also add perf counter for 'coalesced_pages' vs 'per_request_pages'.

jess: will add counters and the bench. tagging @qa for soak next week. :+1:

ellie: summary: root cause = batching heuristic + KV page misalignment -> per-request fetch fallback -> HBM thrash. mitigation = coalesce path + kernel-selector hint. follow-ups: bench + PR + nightly trace alert.

ellie: attaching quick grep output from the run for anyone debugging: ```grep -n "KVFetch.*coalesce=false" /var/log/runner/1952109876.log | wc -l -> 1923``` 

omar: cool. thanks ellie. i'll pick up validation infra.

jess: i'll prep the perf changes.```
